advice: Abstain. The supplied full512 primitive expects the full 512-column B panel and writes a 64-column output tile; it cannot consume a 32-column packed panel while still covering all of C. The panel32 primitive narrows rows, not columns, and does not solve that mismatch. A legal proposal would require a new matching consumer, which is not supplied. Do not infer a benefit from packed access alone. Preserve the fixed ABI, FP32 behavior, timing rules, and fallback.
risks: Inventing a kernel or mapping would exceed the supplied evidence and risk incomplete output or incorrect results. Any future compatible consumer must include panel allocation and packing in gemm timing, preserve fresh inputs, and pass correctness checks before the ten validation reports, ten alternating paired controls, existing promotion gate, and held-out check. No performance effect is known.
